newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends mixed, Nov up on bull spreading.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends mixed, Nov up on bull spreading.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended mixed Monday, with November supported by modest bull spreading, CME pit traders said.
Traders were buying November and January and selling those contracts against March, CME traders said.
Activity was described as very quiet as the trade waited for Canada to issue lumber quotas this week, traders and analysts said.
"Canada is going to be deciding on the quotas this week, so that's what has got everyone so terrified right now," said Tim Elrod, trader and analyst with Pacific Futures Trading.
Elrod said November lumber was poised to test $430.00 to $440.00 per thousand board feet after the decision is announced, and March lumber should test $550.00 per tbf by that contract's expiration.
Lumber futures continued to be underpinned by strong cash markets, Elrod said.
CME lumber futures ended down $4.40 to up $3.20, with November up $3.20 at $421.20 tbf, and January down $2.40 at $388.00.
